1.
The instant interlocutory application has been filed for condonation of delay of 99 days which has occurred in filing the instant appeal.
2. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the instant interlocutory application may be allowed by condoning the delay of 99 days which has occurred in filing the instant appeal.
3. There is no objection on behalf of the respondents to the delay condonation application.
4. This Court, considering the statement so made in the instant interlocutory application, is of the view that the delay which has occurred in filing the appeal needs to be condoned.

5. Accordingly, the delay of 99 days is hereby, condoned and the instant interlocutory application stands allowed, as such, disposed of.
L.P.A. No. 437 of 2023:
6.

The instant intra-court appeal has been filed under Clause 10 of the Letters Patent against the order/judgment dated 15.03.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court in W.P.(C) No. 5580 of 2021, whereby and whereunder, the learned Single Judge has declined to pass positive direction with respect to enhancement of quantum of compensation in lieu of acquisition of land under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the Act, 2013).
7.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is evident from the factual aspect that the land in question has been acquired in pursuance of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the award has been passed.
The appellants being not satisfied with the quantum of amount of compensation, have made an application for its enhancement.
The same has been referred before the Settlement Authority in view of the provision of Section 62 of the Act, 2013.

The learned Single Judge, after taking into consideration the fact that the main issue of enhancement of compensation has already been referred before the authority as constituted and as provided under the Act, 2013, as such has declined to pass positive direction in favour of the appellants which is under challenge in this intra-court appeal.

8. This Court, considering the aforesaid fact, is of the view that since the grievance of the appellants pertaining to enhancement of the amount of compensation was already in seisin before the concerned appropriate authority and if the learned Single Judge, in that view of the matter, has refused to pass positive direction in favour of the appellants, the same according to the considered Ganesh Ramani vs The State Of Jharkhand on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197073891/
